title: JSON functions in queries
summary: Build and consume JSON in T-SQL with JSON_OBJECT, JSON_ARRAY, JSON_ARRAYAGG, and FOR JSON.

items: Serialize result sets with FOR JSON.

blocks.body: Beyond reading JSON, T-SQL can construct it — essential for API and RAG payloads (Domain 3).

terms.definition: Clause that serializes a query result set into JSON (PATH or AUTO).
Aggregates values from multiple rows into a JSON array.

blocks.body: `JSON_OBJECT('k':v,...)` and `JSON_ARRAY(...)` build documents; `JSON_ARRAYAGG`/`JSON_OBJECTAGG` aggregate rows; `FOR JSON PATH` shapes nested output. These directly feed language-model prompts when you convert structured rows to JSON.

tips: FOR JSON PATH with ROOT() wraps output in a named root object.
This lesson links to RAG: converting rows to JSON for a model.

blocks.body: Construct JSON with the constructors and FOR JSON; you'll reuse this to feed models in RAG workflows.
